facts.raw_span: 4 months of progressively worsening symmetric pain in the small joints of her hands, wrists, knees, and ankles
early morning stiffness lasting 2 hours daily
severe fatigue throughout the day
mild COVID-19 infection confirmed by SARS-CoV-2 PCR
denied fever, chills, night sweats, weight loss, rash, or appetite changes since recovering
erythrocyte sedimentation rate of 13 mm/hour
C-reactive protein of 4.3 mg/L
antinuclear antibody titer of 1:640
rheumatoid factor of 62.29 IU/mL
anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody of 237.39 units
MRI of the hands demonstrated synovitis of the bilateral distal radioulnar joints and the left second metacarpophalangeal joint
tenosynovitis around the extensor carpi ulnaris tendon

concepts.why: The patient's symptoms of symmetric pain in the small joints, early morning stiffness, and elevated rheumatoid factor and anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody levels are consistent with Rheumatoid Arthritis, and the MRI findings of synovitis and tenosynovitis further support this diagnosis.

The patient's symptoms of fatigue, joint pain, and elevated antinuclear antibody titer are consistent with Systemic Lupus Erythematosus, although the absence of other typical SLE features and the presence of rheumatoid factor and anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody make this diagnosis less likely.

The patient's recent history of COVID-19 infection and the development of symmetric joint pain and stiffness, along with the MRI findings of synovitis and tenosynovitis, are consistent with Post-COVID-19 Reactive Arthritis, although the presence of rheumatoid factor and anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody is not typical of this condition.

The patient's symptoms of joint pain, fatigue, and elevated antinuclear antibody titer, along with the absence of other typical features of Rheumatoid Arthritis or Systemic Lupus Erythematosus, are consistent with Mixed Connective Tissue Disease, although this diagnosis is less likely given the presence of rheumatoid factor and anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody.

The patient's symptoms of joint pain, fatigue, and elevated antinuclear antibody titer, along with the absence of other typical features of Rheumatoid Arthritis or Systemic Lupus Erythematosus, are consistent with Undifferentiated Connective Tissue Disease, although this diagnosis is less specific and would require further evaluation to confirm.
